cards.title: Set Up a TikTok Business Center and Advertiser Account Cleanly
cards.summary: Create a dedicated TikTok Business Center with a business-domain email, verified advertiser account and backup payment method before spending on ads.
cards.use_when: You are launching a store's first TikTok ads and need foundational account infrastructure that supports smoother approvals and billing.
steps: Go to business.tiktok.com and click Get Started; sign up with a business email address rather than a personal one, because TikTok reportedly gives better ad approval rates with business domains.
Even if you already have a personal TikTok account, register with email and password so personal and business identities stay separate.
In the Business Center, add billing information, then click Add an Advertiser Account and create a new one; complete the business name and verification prompts.
Open Payment Management > Settings and add a credit card first for faster approval.
Add a backup payment method such as PayPal so a failed card debit does not trigger ad disapprovals.
Verify the current TikTok interface and any regional verification requirements, since the exact menu labels and steps change over time.
caveats: The approval-rate advantage for business domains is the presenter's recommendation, not an independently verified benchmark.
Exact URLs and menu names may change; confirm in the live ads manager.

cards.title: Install the TikTok Pixel Through Shopify Partner Integration
cards.summary: Install the TikTok Pixel via partner integration and confirm core conversion events such as complete payment are tracking before launch.
cards.use_when: You are preparing a Shopify store to run TikTok conversion campaigns and need reliable purchase event tracking.
steps: In Ads Manager, open Tools > Events > Get Started Web and select your website.
Choose Partner Integrations rather than manual setup when Shopify or Google Tag Manager is available, because partner syncing is simpler.
Authorize access and complete the onboarding flow; wait the short sync period.
Confirm the pixel shows as active on the right-hand side of the events screen, and verify core conversion events such as complete payment are being received.
If no partner integration is available, use manual setup and follow the on-screen instructions.
Verify the current interface, as event names and setup paths can change.
caveats: Pixel verification is a prerequisite; do not assume events are flowing just because installation appeared to succeed.
Partner integrations may not cover every store setup or region.

cards.title: Use the Three-Tier Campaign Pyramid for TikTok Ads
cards.summary: Structure TikTok campaigns as objective-level campaigns, experiment-level ad groups and creative-level ads to keep testing organized and scalable.
cards.use_when: You are building or restructuring a TikTok ad account for a product store and want clear separation between objectives, audiences and creatives.
steps: Create one campaign per main objective (for example, web conversions for a product store, lead generation for email capture, or traffic for early creative testing).
Under each campaign, create multiple ad groups that each control budget, targeting, schedule and bid, treating each ad group as a mini experiment testing something specific.
Inside each ad group, place multiple ad creatives (videos, copy, CTAs) so you can compare creative variations within the same audience and budget.
Avoid dumping your entire budget into a single ad group; spread spend across several experiment ad groups.
When reviewing results, judge each ad group independently, because the algorithm learns separately at the ad group level and a losing ad group does not drag down a winning one.
Use a naming convention covering product, objective and date (for example, 'shoes-conversion-Feb-04') to keep reporting readable.
Verify current UI naming, since TikTok periodically renames objectives and settings.
caveats: The source's claimed separation of ad group learning is based on the presenter's client experience, not published TikTok documentation.
This structure is a starting heuristic; high-spend accounts may consolidate ad groups differently.

cards.title: Configure a Conversion Ad Group with Broad Targeting and $50/Day
cards.summary: Set up a web-conversion ad group with pixel-based complete payment optimization, TikTok-only placement, broad demographic targeting and at least $50/day.
cards.use_when: You are creating the first TikTok conversion ad group for a store and need concrete settings and a defensible minimum budget.
steps: In the ad group, select your installed pixel under Data Connection and choose 'complete payment' (or another deep purchase event) as the optimization event.
Set Manual Placement and untick everything except TikTok if you want to focus on the main feed first.
Choose location (for example, United States) and a basic age range such as 18–35; keep gender generic and leave other targeting broad so the algorithm can find buyers.
Set the budget to at least $50 per day per ad group; the source argues lower spend will never generate enough data to identify what works.
Leave the schedule continuous rather than time-of-day optimization until you have evidence for scheduling changes.
Change the optimization goal from value to conversions.
Verify current optimization goal and placement labels in the live interface before launching.
caveats: The $50/day minimum is the presenter's stated heuristic after managing over $5M in TikTok spend for clients; it is not a platform guarantee.
Broad targeting assumes enough country-level audience volume; small markets may need broader settings.

cards.title: Build Three Custom Audiences, Then Lookalikes Instead of Direct Retargeting
cards.summary: Create 180-day web visitors, 30-day video completers and uploaded customer files as seeds, then use lookalike audiences in cold ad groups rather than targeting the seeds directly.
cards.use_when: You have a Shopify store with pixel traffic, video views or customer data and want to build TikTok audiences for prospecting campaigns.
steps: In Tools > Audience Manager, click Create Audience > Custom Audience.

Build three seed audiences: (1) web traffic page views in the last 180 days, (2) engagement audience of people who completed your videos in the last 30 days (100% watch), and (3) an uploaded customer CSV.
Name them clearly, such as '180 days web visitors', '30 days video views' and 'customer file'.
Do not target these seeds directly; instead click Create Lookalike Audience and select each custom audience as the source.

Set the lookalike location to the country you are targeting and generally use the 'balanced' setting for large markets like the U.S.; use broad for small markets such as Finland to keep the pool large enough to spend.
In the ad group, add the lookalike audience under Include Audience to tell TikTok to find more people similar to your seed.
Verify current audience manager options, as retention windows and lookalike settings are interface-dependent.
caveats: Retention windows and lookalike expansion options are platform-specific and can change; the 180-day and 30-day windows are the presenter's recommendations.
If seed audiences are very small, lookalikes may be ineffective.

cards.title: Keep Interest Targeting to Two or Three Broad Parent Categories
cards.summary: Limit TikTok interest targeting to a few broad parent categories because stacking 15+ interests raises spend and constrains the algorithm.
cards.use_when: You are setting interest targeting for a TikTok conversion ad group and are tempted to stack many detailed interests.
steps: Select no more than two to three broad, related interests, such as 'fashion and accessories' for an apparel store.
Choose parent categories rather than drilling into many sub-interests, so TikTok's algorithm can identify buyers.

Use the source's example as orientation: a fashion brand started with over 15 detailed interests and saw cost per result above $100 consistently; after stripping down to one broad fashion category, the source reports CPA dropped to 34–41 (currency unit not specified).
Treat this as a case study, not a promise; your category, price point and creative quality affect results.
Pair with behavioral targeting sparingly; the source generally uses only one behavior setting such as iOS 8 and above.
caveats: The reported CPA drop is a specific client case from the presenter's agency, not a general TikTok benchmark.
Broad interest targeting is a current recommendation; seasonal or niche products may need different treatment.

cards.title: Use a Four-Week Targeting Ladder to Refine Audiences Without Overspending
cards.summary: Start broad in week one and add one layer of targeting per week—basic interest, then lookalikes, then stacked winners—to gather data while controlling costs.
cards.use_when: You are launching or scaling a TikTok campaign and want a structured sequence for audience refinement instead of guessing all targeting at once.
steps: Week 1: run broad targeting with only location and basic age range.
Week 2: add one basic interest category that matches the product niche.
Week 3: introduce lookalike audiences built from your custom audience seeds (see the custom/lookalike card).
Week 4: stack winning audiences that performed in earlier weeks, combining lookalikes and proven interests.
Keep budget at the ad group level so each week's tests remain independently readable.
Use the weekly data to decide whether to keep, refine or kill audience configurations rather than making all changes at once.
caveats: The ladder is the presenter's current recommendation; the optimal pace depends on spend volume and how quickly your ad groups accumulate enough impressions.
Do not stack audiences before you have enough spend to learn from each testing layer.

cards.title: Apply the 3:3 Creative Testing Framework Across Hooks, Angles and CTAs
cards.summary: Test three hooks, three angles and three CTAs per product, with at least three distinct ad styles, to find converting creative combinations.
cards.use_when: You have a product to advertise on TikTok and need a structured creative testing plan rather than random video variations.
steps: For each product, create at least three distinct ad styles: a solution/problem video, a tutorial-style video and a lifestyle/UGC-testimonial video.
Within those, vary three hooks, three angles and three CTAs so each test has clear separation between variables.
Test the same creatives against different audiences, because the source reports some creatives bomb with cold traffic but perform well with warm traffic.
Use the winning hooks, angles and CTAs to build the next round of variations rather than changing everything at once.
Verify the current ad creation interface for how to duplicate or vary creatives across ad groups.
caveats: The '3:3 method' is the presenter's internal framework; the specific number of variations may need adjusting for lower budgets or smaller catalogs.
Results depend on product-market fit, offer and landing page, not creative variation alone.

cards.title: Structure a 3:2:1 Test: Three Creatives, Two Audiences, One Objective
cards.summary: Run a first test with three distinct ad creatives, two audience types and one clear objective over three to four days for roughly $300–400 total.
cards.use_when: You are launching a first paid test for a store and need a concrete test plan with budget, duration and audience options.
steps: Set the objective to a single clear conversion goal, such as web conversions or complete payment.
Allocate at least $50 per ad group per day for three to four days, giving a total test budget around $300–400.
Creative one: pain-solution video with the pain point as hook, a demo of the solution and a clear CTA.
Creative two: tutorial-style video with a how-to format, feature highlights and an educational angle.
Creative three: UGC testimonial with real results, before-and-after and an authentic feel.
Audience one: broad interest-based targeting using one or two relevant interests, no age restriction or demographic narrowing.
Audience two: lookalike audience based on purchases, narrowed to top markets such as the U.S. or U.K., with no extra restrictions.
Use distinct styles so the test has clear winners and losers rather than marginal differences.
caveats: The 3:2:1 structure and $300–400 budget are the presenter's recommended test; smaller stores may need to run shorter or lower-budget tests.
The source says this framework generated over eight figures in sales for their clients; treat as a case example, not a guarantee.

cards.title: Check Core TikTok Metrics in the First 24–72 Hours
cards.summary: Use early CTR, watch time and CPM thresholds to diagnose whether a TikTok ad is failing on creative, audience or hook before spending more.
cards.use_when: You have launched a TikTok ad group and need a fast, structured read on whether to fix, kill or scale it.
steps: Within the first 24 hours, check that CTR is above 1%, watch time is above 25% and CPM is under $15.
After three days, look for CPC under $2, add-to-cart cost below $10 and purchase cost under $30.
If CTR is below 1% within 24 hours, treat it as a creative problem and produce a stronger hook or transitions.
If CPM is above $20, treat it as an audience problem and adjust targeting.
If watch time is below 20%, treat the hook as insufficient and create variations of the first three seconds.
Kill the bottom 50% of ads after three days and double down on the winners with new variations.
Do not optimize any ad before spending at least $50 or reaching 1,000 impressions, because the data is not yet meaningful.
Verify current metric benchmarks, as the presenter's thresholds are TikTok-specific snapshots and may vary by market and product.
caveats: These thresholds (CTR >1%, watch time >25%, CPM <$15, CPC <$2, ATC <$10, purchase <$30) are the presenter's current heuristics, not universal benchmarks.
The $50 or 1,000-impression minimum is the source's stated floor for statistical significance; it does not guarantee a reliable read.

cards.title: Use the Diagnostic Checklist to Separate Creative Problems from Audience Problems
cards.summary: Map specific early performance failures to the right fix: weak hook, creative transitions or audience targeting.
cards.use_when: A TikTok ad group is underperforming and you need to decide whether to change the creative or the targeting before spending more.
steps: If CTR is low (below 1% in the first 24 hours), replace the creative with a stronger hook and better transitions rather than changing audiences first.
If CPM is high (above $20), adjust audience targeting and broaden or refine the audience setup; do not assume the creative is the sole cause.
If watch time is low (below 20%), remake the first three seconds specifically rather than overhauling the whole video.
Continue to check each metric independently within the first 24–72 hours, since multiple issues can coexist.
After three days, if the ad group is still weak, kill the bottom 50% and reinvest into winners instead of repeatedly patching failing creative.
Verify current platform reporting, as metric windows and definitions can change.
caveats: The thresholds are the presenter's stated TikTok benchmarks; different categories and markets may perform differently.
A low CTR can also result from poor product-market fit or a mismatched landing page, which the diagnostic does not cover.

cards.title: Use Native Video Formats and the Five Highest-Converting Hook Patterns
cards.summary: Make TikTok ads that look like organic content using UGC, POV or tutorial formats, and open with one of five hook patterns to stop the scroll.
cards.use_when: You are creating ad creative for a store on TikTok and need formats and hook patterns that match the platform rather than TV-style ads.
steps: Choose from the three formats the source says are performing: UGC, POV story and tutorial/how-to video.
Avoid making ads look like TV commercials; the moment content looks like an ad, viewers scroll past.
Open with one of five hook patterns: pattern interruption, controversial statement, curiosity gap, visual hook or time-based hook.
Aim to stop the scroll in the first three seconds and deliver on the hook's implied 'what's in it for me' quickly.
Use text overlays for silent viewers, fast pacing and multiple micro-CTAs throughout the video.
Verify current TikTok creative best practices, as formats and trending patterns change quickly.
caveats: The source's format and hook lists are current observations from the presenter's agency, not fixed platform rules.
Avoid claims or visuals that violate TikTok ad policies; native-looking creative still must comply with platform rules.

cards.title: Follow the 0–35 Second Ad Structure and Technical Specs
cards.summary: Build TikTok ads in four timed sections—hook, promise, proof, CTA—and meet minimum video specs such as 9:16 and 15–35 seconds.
cards.use_when: You are scripting and producing a TikTok ad for a store and want a concrete structure and export settings.
steps: Structure the first 0–3 seconds as the hook.
Use 3–15 seconds for the core promise or problem.
Use 15–30 seconds for proof and demonstration.
Use the final 30–35 seconds for the call to action.
Layer pattern interrupts every two seconds, text overlays for silent viewers and multiple micro-CTAs throughout the video.
Use emotional triggers such as before/after, transformations or validations.
Export at 9:16 aspect ratio (1080 x 1920), keep the file under 500 MB, and aim for a video length of 15–30 seconds; the source says their sweet spot is around 32 seconds.
Keep cuts every two to three seconds, use trending sounds from TikTok's library where appropriate, keep background music at most 80% volume and voiceover at -3 dB, and add captions for accessibility.
caveats: The 'sweet spot' length of 32 seconds is the presenter's finding, not a universal rule.
Technical specs such as 1080 x 1920, codec and file size may change; confirm current TikTok upload requirements.
Trending sounds for ads may have commercial-use restrictions; the source later notes using commercial music in CapCut for ads.

cards.title: Build a High-Retention Ad with an Undeniable Hook and Rhythmic Editing
cards.summary: Analyze a 30M-view TikTok ad to learn how a curiosity-driven hook, promised payoff and varied clip rhythm can sustain retention.
cards.use_when: You are editing a TikTok ad for a store and want to increase watch time and rewatch rate through pacing and payoff structure.
steps: Open with a hook that implies a clear 'what's in it for me', such as revealing an underrated resource or tool.
Keep the hook short—around two seconds—and deliver on its promise quickly so viewers feel rewarded.
Cut clips at varied lengths (some 3 seconds, some half a second) to create rhythm and avoid monotony.
Vary the audio and visual cadence: alternate speaking and silence, zoom in and out, and accelerate clips to create fast-to-slow pacing.
End by delivering the promised payoff, such as showing the actual tool or result.
If retention is the priority, test ads without a spoken call to action; the source says CTAs can damage retention and rewatch rate, and TikTok automatically adds a clickable button.
Verify current features, as automatic ad buttons and retention metrics are platform-dependent.
Note: the 30M views, 2.3M likes and 7% CTR are specific results from the source's client, not a guarantee.
caveats: The recommendation to omit a verbal CTA is the presenter's opinion based on retention metrics; it may not apply to every product or campaign objective.
Retention is one factor among many; conversion still depends on offer, landing page and product fit.

cards.title: Edit UGC-Style TikTok Ads in CapCut with the Agency Formula
cards.summary: Use CapCut to trim hooks, apply a 4K filter, add hook text, add commercially safe music and export at 1080p with a defined workflow.
cards.use_when: You are producing TikTok ad creative in-house and need a repeatable editing workflow with specific settings.
steps: Film clips with natural window light, a clean background, phone held vertically, in 3–5 second segments and from multiple angles.
In CapCut, create a project, drag in raw clips and click Adapt to convert everything to 9:16 vertical format.
Apply the 4K filter across the entire timeline as the base effect for UGC-style ads.
Trim the first clip to a maximum of three seconds and make it the strongest hook.

Add text over the hook clip using a readable font such as Gilroy Semi Bold or your brand font; adjust tracking tighter, position the text just above eye level and add a subtle stroke or outline if visibility is poor.
Apply a typewriter text animation to the hook text as a small pattern interrupt.
Add background music from CapCut's commercial music section—not TikTok sounds—to keep usage commercially safe; lower music to 70% if using a voiceover.
Export at 1080p, H.264, MP4, 60 fps and recommended bit rate. Always preview on a phone before uploading.
Structure the ad as hook, problem, solution, call to action and ensure text and pacing reflect that sequence.
caveats: CapCut's interface, filter names and export settings may change; verify the current app version.
The source recommends CapCut because it is free and TikTok-owned, but other editors can produce equivalent results.
Commercial music availability and licensing terms can change.

cards.title: Use a Naming Convention and Avoid Smart Campaigns for Cleaner Testing
cards.summary: Name campaigns by product, objective and date, and toggle off smart campaigns to preserve manual control over ad group testing.
cards.use_when: You are creating TikTok campaigns for a store and need reporting clarity plus full control over testing variables.
steps: Before launching, define a naming convention: product, objective and date (for example, 'shoes-conversion-Feb-04').
On the campaign creation screen, toggle off smart campaigns so you retain flexibility over ad group structure.
Apply the convention consistently across campaigns, ad groups and ads so labels stay readable in reporting.
Use the naming to quickly identify which product, objective and test date each row belongs to when reviewing performance.
Verify current TikTok naming and smart campaign options, as the interface and defaults change.
caveats: Smart campaigns may be useful in some accounts; the source recommends disabling them for the testing structure described.
Naming conventions are internal process, not a platform feature.

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a complete A-to-Z execution guide for setting up TikTok ad accounts, structuring three-tier campaigns (Campaigns, Ad Groups, Ads), configuring Shopify pixel integrations, building custom and lookalike audiences, and deploying structured multi-variable creative testing frameworks. modules: [ADC] topics: [campaign setup and tracking, algorithm mechanics, return on ad spend (ROAS)] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. campaign setup and tracking / Establishing foundational TikTok ad infrastructure properly by creating a dedicated Business Center using a business email domain to ensure better ad approval rates. Configuring advertiser accounts, establishing secure payment methods with backups, and installing the TikTok Pixel via partner integrations (Shopify) to track core conversion events like complete payment. Structuring campaigns using a clean three-tier pyramid (Campaigns for objectives, Ad Groups for budgets/targeting/bidding, and Ads for creative assets), allocating at least $50/day per ad group to provide the algorithm with sufficient data. algorithm mechanics / Leveraging TikTok's algorithmic learning capabilities by keeping audience targeting broad (e.g., location and basic age ranges) to let the platform's AI identify buyers. Constructing custom audiences from website visitors (180 days), video viewers (30 days), and uploaded customer files, and using them as seed sources to build balanced lookalike audiences. return on ad spend (ROAS) / Implementing systematic creative testing frameworks (such as the "3:3 method"—testing 3 hooks, 3 angles, and 3 CTAs) with strict evaluation thresholds. Monitoring primary metrics within the first 24 to 72 hours (CTR above 1%, watch time above 25%, CPM under $15) and utilizing a diagnostic checklist to fix creative problems (weak hooks/transitions) versus audience problems based on specific performance failures.

Look for. The primary reason to use a business email domain when setting up a TikTok Business Center: it improves ad approval rates. The recommended minimum daily budget per ad group on TikTok to ensure the algorithm gathers enough data: at least $50 per day. The diagnostic rule for a low Click-Through Rate (CTR) within the first 24 hours: a CTR below 1% indicates a creative problem that requires a stronger hook or better transitions.

Skip. Promotional pitches to book a marketing agency call or claim external TikTok ad credit links.

Scope mix. Almost all core.

Volume. 15 to 20.
